title: kith-jmap: role-before-handler dispatch order is correct security design
description: Dispatcher::dispatch_one() performs the role check against METHOD_ROLES BEFORE looking up the handler. This is correct defense-in-depth: the comment says 'Role check MUST precede handler lookup (defense-in-depth)'. An attacker calling a peer-only method as owner gets forbidden, not unknownMethod, regardless of handler registration state. The two separate handler maps (handlers for owner, peer_handlers for peer) with the typed-identity parameter on PeerJmapHandler::call() is a good API design: it makes it impossible for a peer handler to forget to check the caller identity because the identity is injected as a typed parameter rather than being extractable from args.
